exports.text: Without pin control support, consumer calls degrade safely: acquiring a handle or looking up a state returns null, selecting a state or choosing a power state reports success, and releasing a handle does nothing. Managed and unmanaged variants share this fallback.
GPIO helpers report lines usable and accept request, direction and configuration changes with success, while release is ignored when pin control is unavailable.
Board mapping registration reports success without storing entries, and unregistration plus dummy provisioning are empty when the core is disabled.

hazards.text: Two names share 0x360c, the FBD CNB function and the I7300 error function, so matching must treat them as aliases for one value rather than distinct devices.

Several values are overloaded and need context: AXP64 equals Alpha64 and ARMv7 equals ARMNT and hybrid x86 equals CHPE x86; thunk and container share 0x1000; protected and no-defer share 0x4000; far-data and pointer-relative share 0x8000; purgeable, 16-bit, locked and preload meanings vary by processor.

Parsers must bound the DOS message against file length, treat eight-byte section names as possibly unterminated or indirection encoded, and validate directory, section and relocation counts before indexing. Fallback shims returning null or success can mask missing hardware if callers ignore disabled builds.

invariants.text: PCI vendor, device, subvendor and subdevice numbers are stable 16-bit bus identifiers grouped by vendor. Drivers match on vendor plus device and optionally sub-identifiers, covering host bridges, memory controllers, I/O hubs, audio, graphics and accelerators, so values must never be renumbered.
Five series 3400 LPC identifiers form an inclusive interval from MIN 0x3b00 to MAX 0x3b1f; valid family values span that range.

The PE header is guarded against multiple inclusion. Signature, machine, characteristic, subsystem and section numbers describe an on-disk format shared with firmware and loaders, so assignments are fixed interface facts.
Frame helpers round an address up to a page boundary, shift a frame number left to a byte address, and shift a byte address right to a frame number using page size, mask and shift.
The personality reader isolates selected bits with a mask constant, while the writer stores the supplied value into the current task field.
Mapping helpers build static entries for dummy states, mux selections and pin or group configs, with shorthand supplying default state name, self-hosted controller or array length.

state_machines.text: Combined helpers offer acquire plus activate by state name with default shorthand in managed and unmanaged flavors; success transfers ownership to the caller, while lookup or activation failure releases partial state and propagates an error.

structs.text: DOS stub holds 16-bit words for block size, page counts, relocation count, header sizes, stack and instruction pointers, checksum, table offset, overlay and OEM fields, then a 32-bit PE offset and variable message bytes. Each DOS relocation pairs a 16-bit offset with a 16-bit segment.
COFF file header starts with a 32-bit signature, then machine and section counts, timestamp, symbol table location and count, optional header length and a flag word.

32-bit optional header carries linker versions, code and data sizes, entry offset, code and data bases, load address, alignments, version fields, sizes, checksum, subsystem and loader flags, stack and heap reservations and directory count. The 64-bit form omits the data base and widens addresses and reservations.

Data directory is sixteen address-plus-size pairs in fixed order covering exports, imports, resources, exceptions, certificates, relocations, debug, architecture, global pointer, TLS, load config, bound imports, import addresses, delay imports, runtime header and reserved, each address relative to load base.

Section entry holds an eight-byte name that may encode a string-table offset, loaded size, virtual address, raw size, file pointers to data, relocations and line numbers, 16-bit counts and a 32-bit characteristic word.
COFF relocation holds virtual address and symbol index as 32-bit words plus a 16-bit type selector interpreted per architecture for x64, ARM, SH, PowerPC, x86 and IA64 vocabularies or as a raw value.
Certificate header is eight bytes with a 32-bit total length and 16-bit revision and type selectors.

Pin mapping identifies consumer device, desired state, mapping kind and controller, with payload either mux group plus function names or target pin or group plus configuration array length and pointer. Kinds order invalid, dummy, mux, per-pin configs and per-group configs.

Early Intel identifiers are fixed, including PCI_DEVICE_ID_INTEL_82801DB_12 takes 0x24cc and PCI_DEVICE_ID_INTEL_82801EB_0 takes 0x24d0 and PCI_DEVICE_ID_INTEL_82820_HB takes 0x2500 and PCI_DEVICE_ID_INTEL_E7501_MCH takes 0x254c and PCI_DEVICE_ID_INTEL_82845G_HB takes 0x2560 and PCI_DEVICE_ID_INTEL_82865_HB takes 0x2570.

Platform audio and small-vendor numbers are fixed, including Lakefield audio takes 0x98c8 and Lynx Point LP audio takes 0x9c20 and Skylake LP audio takes 0x9d70 and Tiger Lake LP audio takes 0xa0c8 and Wangxun vendor takes 0x8088 and ScaleMP vendor takes 0x8686 and Netmos vendor takes 0x9710.

EFI stub revision is major 3 minor 0. Identification values are Linux magic 0x818223cd and DOS signature 0x5a4d and NT signature 0x4550 and ROM magic 0x107 and 32-bit magic 0x10b and 64-bit magic 0x20b.

Section word reserves bits 20 to 23 for alignment with mask 0x00f00000, stepping from 0x00100000 for one byte to 0x00e00000 for 8192 bytes with 0x00f00000 reserved. High bits are overflow 0x01000000 and discardable 0x02000000 and not cached 0x04000000 and not paged 0x08000000 and shared 0x10000000 and execute 0x20000000 and read 0x40000000 and write 0x80000000.

Certificate types are PKCS signed data 0x0002 and EFI OKCS115 0x0EF0 and EFI GUID 0x0EF1 with revisions 0x0100 and 0x0200. Relocation vocabularies start at zero for absolute and increase in order, holding x64 17 values through SSPAN32 and ARM 7 through SECREL and SH 26 through NOMODE and PowerPC 18 through TOKEN and x86 11 through REL32 and IA64 29 through ADDEND.
